statement: In the deterministic setting just defined, assume the following. (i) (πn)∗µn ⇒ µ, and the maximum projected edge length tends to zero: max {v,w}∈E(Gn) d0(πn(v), πn(w)) −→ 0. (ii) Every uniformly convergent sequence with continuous limit u satisfies lim inf n en(un) ≥ Z |∇u|2 dA, where the right side is +∞ unless u ∈ W1,2(S2). Every smooth u has a uniformly convergent recovery sequence with energy tending to that integral. 51 (iii) For every open U ⊂ S2, sequences that are graph-harmonic at all vertices in π−1 n (U) and have uniformly bounded supremum and total energy are locally equicontinuous in U under πn, and locally uniformly precompact there. Here equicontinuity means that, for every compact K ⊂ U, lim δ↓0 lim sup n sup πn(v),πn(w)∈K d0(πn(v),πn(w))≤δ |un(v) − un(w)| = 0, and precompactness means uniform comparison with a continuous function on each compact subset after a common subsequence. (iv) For the centered solution operator HnGng = µng, µn(Gng) = 0, µn(g) = 0, there are constants C < ∞ and ρ > 0, independent of n, such that ∥Gng∥∞ ≤ C µn(|g|)ρ if ∥g∥∞ ≤ 1 and µn(g) = 0. (7.3) Then the laws of (πn(Y n t ))0≤t≤T , with initial law µn, converge in D([0, T], S2) to the law of (Bt)0≤t≤T , for every finite T. The limit has continuous paths. In addition, for every α > 0 and f ∈ C(S2), the resolvents converge uniformly under πn.
